verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. The paper introduces a named predicate — a smooth scalar or vector g is `flat at the radial edge X_e ∈ {X_a, X_b}` iff componentwise ∂_X^j g(X_e,η) = 0 for every j ≥ 0 and every η ∈ [−1,1]. No declaration defining such a predicate was found; the repository states the property one function at a time, in two unrelated encodings. (a) For the paper's edge weight ζ — `LeadingStressWeights.zeta`, whose body is `radialWeight (activationTime^2) (leftEdge W) (rightEdge W)` — `radialWeight_flat_left/right` state `iteratedDeriv n (radialWeight c a b) (Real.exp a) = 0` and `… (Real.exp b) = 0` for every n : ℕ, at X_e = exp(leftEdge W) = X_a and exp(rightEdge W) = X_b. That is literally the paper's formula for this g: n ranges over all of ℕ so j = 0 is included (and indeed radialWeight vanishes at the edge), and the η quantifier is vacuous because radialWeight is a function of X alone. So Theorem 4.6(iv)'s use of the notion (`every radial derivative of ζ vanishes at X_a, X_b`) is supplied. (b) The η-uniform form is stated only for the model edge factor and only in the edge coordinate x = log(X/X_a) rather than in X: `weighted_iteratedFDeriv_zero` gives, for every parameter p and every n, that the full mixed derivative tensor of `weighted c j B` vanishes at (p,0) — stronger than the paper's radial-only derivatives, and for arbitrary p rather than p = η ∈ [−1,1], but about that particular function. For the other object the paper calls flat at both edges, the stress T_0, no jets-vanish statement was found: edge flatness of the stress is carried instead by the `EdgeFactor` identity T (p,x) = (FlatCutoff.edge c x / x^order) • coefficient (p,x) (ActiveAnnulusWeight.lean:257-258), used via `LeadingStressWeights.inner_direction` (line 738).
